metadata.title: African Emergency Resuscitation Guideline Directory (v3)
metadata.description: Structured database of standard international clinical consensus guidelines vs. validated local adaptations in resource-limited African settings, complete with bibliography and source URLs.

guidelines.guideline: World Health Organization (WHO) — Emergency Care Toolkit, Basic Emergency Care, trauma, infectious disease, mass-casualty and resource-limited emergency care guidance.
guidelines.global_standard: Aggressive, resource-intensive time-to-treatment targets, routine lab screening, and advanced diagnostics.
guidelines.african_reality: Severe shortages of human resources, lack of blood culture bottles, lactate assays, or ICU ventilators [24, 71].
guidelines.local_adaptation: Implementation of the qSOFA and SATS (South African Triage Scale) for clinical risk stratification. Standardizing 'Assess, Stabilise, Administer, Prioritise' (ASAP) protocols to prioritize high-risk syndromic cohorts.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Under WHO resource-limited standards, clinical triage scales like SATS and simplified clinical warning tools replace missing laboratory profiles to flag sick patients early.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: FEAST Trial (2011) demonstrating 45% increased mortality with aggressive rapid fluid boluses in resource-limited pediatric sepsis.
guidelines.bibliography: World Health Organization. Pocket book of hospital care for children: Guidelines for the management of common childhood illnesses. 2nd edition, Geneva: World Health Organization; 2013.

guidelines.guideline: International Federation for Emergency Medicine (IFEM) — international ED standards, quality and safety frameworks, paediatric ED standards and disaster guidance.
guidelines.global_standard: Rigid facility-level structural requirements, specific ratios of emergency specialists, and specialized pediatric resuscitation zones.
guidelines.african_reality: Widespread rural primary care settings where emergency units are run by general medical officers without emergency specialty training, facing unstable electrical grids and variable oxygen supply.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Focus on standardized basic clinical pathways, task-sharing, and regional simulation-based training (e.g., ESMOE/EOST) rather than fixed physical infrastructure.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We focus on building functional and clinical resilience through task-shifting and emergency drills (such as ESMOE) to optimize outcomes with existing staffing.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: Baelani I, et al. Availability of critical care resources survey.
guidelines.bibliography: Baelani I, Jochberger S, Laimer T, et al. Availability of critical care resources to treat patients with severe sepsis or septic shock in Africa: a self-reported survey of anaesthesia providers. Critical Care. 2011;15(1):R10.

guidelines.guideline: American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) — clinical policies specifically addressing ED patients.
guidelines.global_standard: Rapid diagnostic workups with high-sensitivity serum biomarkers (such as highly sensitive troponins) and immediate CT scans.
guidelines.african_reality: Extremely slow lab turnaround times and lack of CT imaging after hours in district and regional clinics.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Heuristics and diagnostic algorithms based on clinical scores (e.g., Wells score for PE, qSOFA for infection, and ABC score for massive transfusion).
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We use validated clinical risk scores to safely bypass the need for rapid high-cost laboratory markers, directing precious diagnostics only to equivocal cases.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: Andrews B, et al. Early resuscitation protocol randomized trial.
guidelines.bibliography: Andrews B, Semler MW, Muchemwa L, et al. Effect of an early resuscitation protocol on in-hospital mortality among adults with sepsis and hypotension: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2017;318(13):1233-1240.

guidelines.guideline: Royal College of Emergency Medicine (RCEM) — clinical standards covering resuscitation, sedation, trauma, paediatrics, infectious disease and general ED care.
guidelines.global_standard: Strict quality targets including rapid time-to-treatment windows and specific mechanical ventilation standards.
guidelines.african_reality: Severe shortage of critical care infrastructure, where mechanical ventilators are highly scarce and ICU beds are severely limited.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Prioritization of non-invasive ventilatory support (like nasal prongs or face masks) and careful volume-targeted fluid resuscitations.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Because we operate with limited access to mechanical ventilation, our resuscitation guidelines emphasize non-invasive oxygenation and avoiding hyperoxia to prevent respiratory fatigue.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: Mthatha Regional Hospital prospective observational pragmatic cohort study.
guidelines.bibliography: One in four die from acute infectious illness in an emergency department in Eastern Cape Province, South Africa. S Afr Med J. 2020;111(2):e12.

guidelines.guideline: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) — condition-specific and service-delivery guidance covering most major ED presentations.
guidelines.global_standard: Comprehensive service-delivery models with specialized rapid referral networks and direct-to-specialist pathways.
guidelines.african_reality: Long travel distances, prolonged transfer delays, and lack of specialized regional centers.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Strengthening primary stabilization and 'holding phase' protocols within district hospitals to support patients safely for 24-72 hours before transfer.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Since transfer times to tertiary care can be delayed by several days, we optimize local holding protocols to manage complex cases safely at the secondary tier.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: NICE Bacterial Meningitis Guideline South African adaptation.
guidelines.bibliography: FINAL DRAFT Paediatric Clinical Protocol - Western Cape Government. Paediatric Meningitis Protocol. 2017.

guidelines.guideline: American College of Radiology Appropriateness Criteria (ACR-AC) — evidence-based selection of imaging for specific clinical presentations.
guidelines.global_standard: Routine high-resolution Computed Tomography (CT) or Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) as first-line modalities for acute abdominal or chest pain.
guidelines.african_reality: Extremely limited access to CT and zero routine emergency MRI. Imaging is frequently restricted to plain film radiography and basic bedside ultrasound.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Meticulous training in Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) and Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) to guide surgical or resuscitation decisions.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: FAST scans and basic bedside ultrasound are utilized as our primary diagnostic workup to rapidly screen for life-threatening pathology, bypassing missing advanced imaging.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: Wood D, et al. Ultrasound findings in cytotoxic snakebites.
guidelines.bibliography: Wood D, Sartorius B, Hift R. Ultrasound findings in 42 patients with cytotoxic tissue damage following bites by South African snakes. Emerg Med J. 2016;33(7):477-481.

guidelines.guideline: International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation (ILCOR) — international evidence reviews and Consensus on Science with Treatment Recommendations.
guidelines.global_standard: Highly standardized, advanced cardiac life support protocols with post-cardiac arrest targeted temperature management (TTM).
guidelines.african_reality: Inability to perform advanced thermoregulation or targeted therapeutic cooling due to lack of cooling blankets and ICU monitoring equipment.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Focus on high-quality basic CPR, rapid defibrillation, and active avoidance of hyperthermia using basic physical methods (such as tepid sponging).
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We prioritize basic high-quality chest compressions and early defibrillation, while therapeutic hypothermia is adapted to basic, low-resource fever management.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: WSES guidelines for management of surgical sepsis.
guidelines.bibliography: Sartelli M, Kluger Y, Anseloni L, et al. Raising concerns about the Sepsis-3 definitions. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:6.

guidelines.guideline: European Resuscitation Council (ERC) Guidelines 2025 — adult, paediatric and neonatal resuscitation, post-resuscitation care and special circumstances.
guidelines.global_standard: Advanced algorithm-driven resuscitations including real-time end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2) feedback and immediate post-resuscitation coronary angiography.
guidelines.african_reality: Lack of quantitative EtCO2 waveform monitoring and absence of after-hours catheterization laboratories.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Clinical indicators of tube placement (such as bilateral chest expansion, misting of the tube, and clinical surrogates) and immediate medical stabilization.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We rely heavily on robust clinical checks for airway confirmation and focus medical management on treating reversible causes of arrest locally.
guidelines.bibliography: Approach to the diagnosis and management of snakebite envenomation in South Africa in humans. S Afr Med J. 2023;113(6):e1037.

guidelines.guideline: American Heart Association CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care Guidelines 2025 — BLS, ACLS, PALS, neonatal resuscitation and systems of care.
guidelines.global_standard: Mandates real-time CPR quality feedback devices and advanced pediatric post-resuscitation algorithms.
guidelines.african_reality: No access to CPR feedback metrics and severe limitations in pediatric intensive care capacity.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Structured, team-based simulation training and task-sharing to maximize CPR quality through manual observation and strict rotation schedules.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Our CPR quality is optimized through strict, manual rotation schedules and direct visual/tactile monitoring of chest recoil, as feedback devices are unavailable.
guidelines.bibliography: Maternal Collapse: Training in resuscitation. Essential Steps in Managing Obstetric Emergencies (ESMOE). ResearchGate. 2015.

guidelines.guideline: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — adult and paediatric sepsis and septic shock.
guidelines.global_standard: Rigid 1-hour resuscitation bundle prescribing a minimum of 30 mL/kg of crystalloid fluid within the first 3 hours [153].
guidelines.african_reality: The FEAST trial showed that rapid fluid boluses increase relative 48-hour pediatric mortality by 45% in low-resource settings lacking mechanical ventilation [154].
guidelines.local_adaptation: Replacing the 1-hour bundle with the ASAP (Assess, Stabilise, Administer, Prioritise) protocol. Initial fluid volumes are restricted to small, targeted boluses (4 mL/kg or 250-500 mL) [156].
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Aggressive fluid boluses are clinically dangerous without mechanical ventilation. We use conservative fluid resuscitation (4 mL/kg boluses) and track perfusion via capillary refill time.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: FEAST Trial (2011) demonstrating 45% increased mortality with rapid fluid boluses.
guidelines.bibliography: Maitland K, Kiguli S, Opoka RO, et al. Mortality after fluid bolus in African children with severe infection (FEAST). N Engl J Med. 2011;364(26):2483-2495.

guidelines.guideline: Society of Critical Care Medicine (SCCM) — airway, sedation, shock, sepsis, analgesia and other critical-care guidance applicable during ED resuscitation.
guidelines.global_standard: Routine utilization of continuous intravenous anesthetic infusions and objective sedation scales in ventilated patients.
guidelines.african_reality: Extremely limited supply of continuous infusion pumps and lack of dedicated critical care nursing staff.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Intermittent bolus dosing of sedation (e.g., titrated ketamine 1-2 mg/kg/hour or diazepam) and robust visual clinical monitoring [54].
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We utilize careful, bolus-titrated ketamine or diazepam regimens to provide safe, baseline sedation, avoiding continuous infusion pumps which are scarce.
guidelines.bibliography: Approach to the diagnosis and management of snakebite envenomation in South Africa in humans. S Afr Med J. 2023;113(6):e1037.

guidelines.guideline: European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) — critical-care guidelines and international consensus statements.
guidelines.global_standard: Mandatory continuous central venous pressure (CVP) and arterial line monitoring to guide shock therapy.
guidelines.african_reality: Lack of invasive pressure monitoring transducers and arterial cannulas in rural or secondary emergency settings.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Using dynamic bedside clinical assessments, such as the Passive Leg Raise (PLR) test (measuring change in pulse pressure) and capillary refill time [155].
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Since invasive monitors are unavailable, we utilize the Passive Leg Raise (PLR) maneuver as a dynamic, zero-cost test of fluid responsiveness to prevent volume overload.
guidelines.bibliography: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021. Crit Care Med. 2021;49(11):e55.

guidelines.guideline: European Society of Cardiology (ESC) — acute coronary syndromes, pulmonary embolism, aortic disease, arrhythmias, heart failure and hypertensive emergencies.
guidelines.global_standard: Immediate primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) within 90-120 minutes of STEMI diagnosis.
guidelines.african_reality: Absence of coronary catheterization facilities in the public sector outside major metropolitan tertiary centers.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Rapid administration of pharmacological fibrinolysis (such as Tenecteplase or Streptokinase) in the ED within 30 minutes, followed by planned transfer.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Because we operate outside a PCI-capable window, our STEMI protocol focuses on rapid ED fibrinolysis within 30 minutes, unless absolute contraindications exist.
guidelines.bibliography: South African hypertension practice guideline 2014. Cardiovasc J Afr. 2014;25(6):288-294.

guidelines.guideline: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC) — acute cardiovascular disease, arrhythmias, chest pain, pulmonary embolism and heart failure.
guidelines.global_standard: Mandates high-sensitivity troponin assays and rapid-rule-out chest pain pathways (0-hour and 1-hour protocols).
guidelines.african_reality: Turnaround times for serum cardiac markers are frequently 4-12 hours, rendering rapid-rule-out algorithms clinically dangerous.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Adopting the HEART score with standard point-of-care troponin checks and serial ECG monitoring to safely risk-stratify chest pain.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We use the clinical HEART score coupled with bedside point-of-care cardiac markers and serial 12-lead ECGs to guide chest pain disposition under local constraints.
guidelines.bibliography: Seedat YK, Rayner BL. South African hypertension practice guideline 2014. Cardiovasc J Afr. 2014;25(6):288-294.

guidelines.guideline: American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) — acute ischaemic stroke, intracerebral haemorrhage and subarachnoid haemorrhage; the acute ischaemic stroke guideline was updated in 2026.
guidelines.global_standard: Thrombolytic therapy (Alteplase) within 4.5 hours of ischemic stroke onset, and immediate endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusions.
guidelines.african_reality: Extremely limited access to emergency head CT scans after hours and near-total absence of EVT facilities in public hospitals.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Meticulous clinical stroke screening, rapid blood glucose checks to rule out mimic hypoglycemia, and strict SBP management (<185/110 mmHg for thrombolysis candidates).
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Because thrombectomy is unavailable, our priority is rapid clinical screen, ruling out hypoglycemia, and cautious BP titration to protect the penumbra.
guidelines.bibliography: Hypertensive Emergencies - ACCP. Clinical Guidelines. 2018.

guidelines.guideline: CHEST Guidelines — venous thromboembolism, pulmonary embolism and antithrombotic treatment.
guidelines.global_standard: Routine low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for VTE prophylaxis in all hospitalized medical patients.
guidelines.african_reality: High risk of bleeding in patients with undetected parasitic infections, chronic tuberculosis, or advanced HIV disease.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Strict adherence to VTE risk-stratification models, starting prophylactic enoxaparin (40 mg daily) only after ruling out active hemoptysis or bleeding.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We strictly screen for tuberculosis-associated hemoptysis and other systemic bleed risk factors before initiating VTE chemical prophylaxis.
guidelines.bibliography: Guidelines and Protocols of Diabetes Emergencies. Pediatric Protocol. Pediatric Diabetes. 2014.

guidelines.guideline: American Society of Hematology (ASH) — venous thromboembolism, anticoagulation and haematological emergencies.
guidelines.global_standard: Routine use of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) as first-line therapy for acute deep vein thrombosis.
guidelines.african_reality: DOACs are highly expensive and virtually unavailable on the public hospital essential medicines list.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Utilizing standard Warfarin therapy, bridging initially with subcutaneous Enoxaparin, and relying on clinic-based INR monitoring.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Since DOACs are not on the public EML, we initiate a bridged Warfarin regimen and coordinate with local primary clinics for close INR checks.
guidelines.bibliography: Standard Treatment Guidelines and Essential Medicines List for South Africa: hospital level, adults, 2024 edition. National Department of Health; 2024.

guidelines.guideline: American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs Best Practices Guidelines — trauma resuscitation, traumatic brain injury, geriatric trauma and trauma-system care.
guidelines.global_standard: Mandates immediate trauma center transfer, massive transfusion protocols guided by thromboelastography (TEG), and rapid CT scanning.
guidelines.african_reality: No access to TEG/ROTEM in secondary EDs. Red blood cell and plasma products must be rationed carefully due to chronic blood shortages.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Relying on the clinical Assessment of Blood Consumption (ABC) score (scoring mechanism) to trigger MTP, and administering standard 1:1:1 ratios of blood products.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We use the clinical ABC score (SBP, HR, mechanism, FAST) to trigger massive transfusion preemptively, as advanced lab metrics like TEG are absent.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: CRASH-2 Trial and standard Damage Control Resuscitation guidelines.
guidelines.bibliography: Damage Control Resuscitation. PMC - NIH. Journal of Trauma. 2009;23:231-40.

guidelines.guideline: Eastern Association for the Surgery of Trauma (EAST) — evidence-based trauma practice-management guidelines.
guidelines.global_standard: Universal CT angiography or mandatory surgical exploration for any neck injury that penetrates the platysma.
guidelines.african_reality: Mandatory exploration of all platysma-penetrating neck wounds leads to a high rate of non-therapeutic surgeries.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Adopting Selective Non-Operative Management (SNOM). Surgical exploration is restricted to patients with clinical 'hard signs' of vascular or aerodigestive damage (e.g., active bleeding, expanding hematoma, air bubbling) [126, 158].
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We use Selective Non-Operative Management (SNOM). Only hemodynamically unstable patients or those with hard signs undergo immediate surgical exploration.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: Penetrating neck trauma audit at Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital.
guidelines.bibliography: Surgical exploration for penetrating neck trauma - an audit of results in 145 patients. South African Journal of Surgery. 2020;57(4).

guidelines.guideline: World Society of Emergency Surgery (WSES) — emergency general surgery, intra-abdominal infection, appendicitis, trauma and source control.
guidelines.global_standard: Immediate laparoscopy and advanced intra-abdominal source control with high-generation intravenous antibiotics.
guidelines.african_reality: Severe theater backlogs and delayed access to emergency surgery, often with wait times exceeding 12-24 hours for acute appendicitis.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Early administration of standard broad-spectrum antibiotics (such as Ceftriaxone and Metronidazole) and aggressive physiological resuscitation while awaiting theater.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Given emergency theater delays, we utilize early broad-spectrum empirical antibiotics and intensive fluid resuscitation as a bridge to surgical source control.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: WSES guidelines for management of intra-abdominal infections.
guidelines.bibliography: Compliance with the Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines for early resuscitation does not translate into improved outcomes in patients with surgical sepsis in South Africa. S Afr J Surg. 2019;57(4).

guidelines.guideline: American Association for the Surgery of Trauma (AAST) — often produces joint trauma guidelines with WSES.
guidelines.global_standard: Recommends angiographic embolization for hemodynamically stable high-grade splenic or hepatic lacerations.
guidelines.african_reality: Angiographic embolization is completely unavailable in the vast majority of African public secondary hospitals.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Rigid clinical observation in a high-care unit with serial hemoglobin monitoring and a low threshold for open emergency splenectomy if deterioration occurs.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Because angio-embolization is unavailable, high-grade solid organ injuries are managed with serial hemoglobin checks and physical exams, prepared for immediate laparotomy.
guidelines.bibliography: Update on massive transfusion. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 2013;112(1).

guidelines.guideline: Brain Trauma Foundation (BTF) — adult and paediatric severe traumatic brain injury, penetrating TBI and prehospital neurotrauma.
guidelines.global_standard: Mandates intracranial pressure (ICP) monitor placement for all patients with severe TBI (GCS < 9) and abnormal CT scans.
guidelines.african_reality: ICP monitors are completely unavailable in almost all district and regional emergency departments.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Relying on clinical neuro-checks and administering hyperosmolar rescue therapy (3% hypertonic saline 3 mL/kg or 20% mannitol) only if active brain herniation occurs.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: As we cannot monitor ICP invasively, we focus on clinical herniation signs (pupils, bradycardia) and administer hyperosmolar therapy as a life-saving rescue.
guidelines.bibliography: FINAL DRAFT Paediatric Clinical Protocol - Western Cape Government. Paediatric Meningitis Protocol. 2017.

guidelines.guideline: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) — acute asthma assessment and management; current strategy report is GINA 2026.
guidelines.global_standard: Frequent use of high-dose inhaled corticosteroids, rapid peak flow measurements, and early non-invasive positive pressure ventilation.
guidelines.african_reality: Lack of peak flow meters in emergency units and high risk of gastric inflation with non-invasive ventilation.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Relying on simple clinical signs (respiratory rate, accessory muscle use, SpO2) and standard hourly beta-2 agonist nebulizations combined with oral prednisone.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We manage acute severe asthma using standard clinical distress markers to guide aggressive nebulization and systemic corticosteroids.
guidelines.bibliography: Pneumothorax - The Art of Urgent Care. Ghost. 2024.

guidelines.guideline: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) — COPD diagnosis, exacerbations, ventilation and ongoing management; current report is GOLD 2026.
guidelines.global_standard: First-line non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (BiPAP) for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure.
guidelines.african_reality: Severe shortage of BiPAP machines in district hospitals, where hypercapnic patients must often be managed with titrated oxygen.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Extremely cautious oxygen titration via nasal prongs to a strict target of 88-92% to avoid suppressing the hypoxic respiratory drive.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: To prevent hyperoxia-induced hypercapnia in severe COPD, we titrate supplemental oxygen strictly to a target of 88-92% using nasal prongs.
guidelines.bibliography: Conservative management of spontaneous pneumothorax: A review of evidence and guidelines. PMC. 2025.

guidelines.guideline: European Respiratory Society/American Thoracic Society (ERS/ATS) — acute respiratory failure, non-invasive ventilation, severe asthma and respiratory infections.
guidelines.global_standard: Mandatory high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy and continuous arterial blood gas (ABG) monitoring.
guidelines.african_reality: HFNC systems are unavailable in most district hospitals, and ABG syringes or machines are scarce.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Relying on standard low-flow oxygen devices (nasal prongs, non-rebreather face masks) and monitoring gas exchange via pulse oximetry.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Without high-flow nasal therapy, we optimize standard low-flow oxygen delivery and rely on continuous SpO2 targets to maintain safety.
guidelines.bibliography: Adapting the Sepsis 1-Hour Bundle for Resource-Limited Settings: Lessons from Turkana, Kenya. Preprints.org. 2026.

guidelines.guideline: British Thoracic Society/Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (BTS/SIGN) — asthma, pleural disease, oxygen therapy and pneumothorax guidance.
guidelines.global_standard: The BTS 2023 update de-emphasizes radiographic size thresholds, recommending conservative management for stable Primary Spontaneous Pneumothorax (PSP) [179].
guidelines.african_reality: In rural district hospitals, commercial thoracostomy sets are often out of stock, making invasive chest drain insertions difficult.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Stable PSP is observed conservatively with simple analgesia [179]. For symptomatic PSP, manual needle aspiration via a three-way tap is the first-line rescue.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Under BTS 2023, radiographic size does not dictate intervention. Stable pneumothorax is managed conservatively, and manual needle aspiration is preferred over chest drains.
guidelines.bibliography: Conservative management of spontaneous pneumothorax: A review of evidence and guidelines. Bioinformation. 2025;21(3):471-484.

guidelines.guideline: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) — meningitis, pneumonia, urinary infection, skin infection, antimicrobial resistance and infection-specific guidance.
guidelines.global_standard: Immediate lumbar puncture followed by empiric administration of third-generation cephalosporins, vancomycin, and ampicillin for suspected bacterial meningitis.
guidelines.african_reality: High baseline rates of HIV and cryptococcal disease. Empiric antibacterial therapy fails to cover cryptococcal meningitis, which is highly prevalent [46].
guidelines.local_adaptation: Performing rapid Cryptococcal Antigen (CrAg) lateral flow assays on all CSF samples (or serum) and deferring broad-spectrum antibacterial steroids.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Given our high HIV burden, we perform a lumbar puncture early and screen for cryptococcal antigen before blindly administering high-dose antibacterial steroids.
guidelines.bibliography: SAHCS Guideline for the prevention, diagnosis and management of cryptococcal disease among persons living with HIV: Update to in. Southern African HIV Clinicians Society. 2026.

guidelines.guideline: European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (ESCMID) — severe infection, antimicrobial stewardship and resistant organisms, including ED-specific stewardship guidance.
guidelines.global_standard: Mandates patient-specific microbiological cultures and restricted, narrow-spectrum step-down antibiotic therapy.
guidelines.african_reality: Microbiological culture results are severely delayed (often taking 5-7 days), making rapid clinical step-down impossible.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Strict adherence to regional empiric syndromic antibiotic guidelines (e.g., Ceftriaxone for severe community-acquired infections) to cover highly resistant pathogens.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Due to slow culture turnaround times, we initiate robust empiric syndromic antibiotic coverage and rely on clinic-based infectious disease registries.
guidelines.bibliography: One in four die from acute infectious illness in an emergency department in Eastern Cape Province, South Africa. S Afr Med J. 2020;111(2):e12.

guidelines.guideline: WHO infectious-disease guidelines — malaria, tuberculosis, HIV, rabies, cholera, meningitis and outbreak-related diseases.
guidelines.global_standard: Recommends routine, rapid antigen checks for malaria, rapid nucleic acid amplification (GeneXpert) for tuberculosis, and immediate rabies PEP.
guidelines.african_reality: Frequent local stockouts of GeneXpert cartridges or rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) in rural primary health centers [90].
guidelines.local_adaptation: Meticulous clinical risk assessment (NICD rabies guidelines categorizing Bat bites as Category III), and prioritizing RIG infiltration directly into wounds [91].
guidelines.rounding_pitch: In rabies prophylaxis, bat exposure is always Category III. We prioritize immediate wound washing and wound-site RIG infiltration, which must occur within 7 days of vaccination.
guidelines.bibliography: National Guidelines for the Prevention of Rabies in Humans, South Africa. National Department of Health, NICD. 2021.

guidelines.guideline: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) — acute kidney injury, electrolyte abnormalities and kidney replacement therapy. The 2012 AKI guideline remains published while an updated 2026 guideline is being finalised.
guidelines.global_standard: Early initiation of continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for severe AKI with refractory metabolic acidosis or electrolyte derangements [426].
guidelines.african_reality: CRRT is completely unavailable in district and regional hospitals due to lack of consumables and specialized nursing staff [426].
guidelines.local_adaptation: Aggressive conservative management of hyperkalemia (insulin-dextrose infusions, calcium gluconate) and intermittent hemodialysis where available.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Without CRRT, we rely on active pharmacological management of hyperkalemia and establish a holding protocol while coordinating tertiary transfer.
guidelines.bibliography: Surviving sepsis campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021. Critical Care Society of Southern Africa. 2021.

guidelines.guideline: American Diabetes Association/European Association for the Study of Diabetes consensus guidance — diabetic ketoacidosis, hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state and hypoglycaemia.
guidelines.global_standard: Continuous intravenous insulin infusions titrated hourly based on rapid serum ketone and blood gas profiles.
guidelines.african_reality: Hourly blood gas and serum ketone profiles are unfeasible due to reagent stockouts and high laboratory burdens.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Using a standardized adult DKA protocol starting with 1 L of 0.9% NaCl over the first hour, followed by titrated insulin infusions and potassium replacement.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We manage adult DKA with structured hourly clinical monitoring, starting rehydration with 1 L of normal saline, and checking glucose carefully to prevent hypoglycemia.
guidelines.bibliography: Guidelines and Protocols of Diabetes Emergencies. Pediatric Diabetes. 2014.

guidelines.guideline: Endocrine Society — adrenal crisis, severe hyperglycaemia, hyponatraemia and other endocrine emergencies.
guidelines.global_standard: Immediate administration of IV Hydrocortisone (100 mg bolus) and continuous electrolyte monitoring in suspected adrenal crisis.
guidelines.african_reality: Intravenous hydrocortisone is frequently out of stock, and serum electrolyte turnarounds are slow.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Using oral hydrocortisone or intramuscular options where available, with aggressive clinical rehydration using isotonic fluids.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We manage suspected adrenal crisis with immediate fluid resuscitation and prioritize alternative steroid formulations when IV hydrocortisone is unavailable.
guidelines.bibliography: Standard Treatment Guidelines and Essential Medicines List for South Africa: hospital level, adults, 2024 edition. National Department of Health; 2024.

guidelines.guideline: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) — febrile infants, bronchiolitis, head injury, seizures and other paediatric emergencies.
guidelines.global_standard: Extensive laboratory septic screens (including lumbar puncture, blood cultures, urinalysis) for all febrile infants under 28 days.
guidelines.african_reality: Overwhelming patient volumes and lack of emergency laboratory capacity, making routine extensive screening unfeasible.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Using clinical risk triage scores (e.g., SATS Pediatric Triage) and empirical antibiotic administration for high-risk febrile infants.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We prioritize high-risk febrile infants using validated pediatric clinical triage indicators, initiating empiric antibiotics promptly when clinical signs indicate severe risk.
guidelines.bibliography: FINAL DRAFT Paediatric Clinical Protocol - Western Cape Government. Paediatric Meningitis Protocol. 2017.

guidelines.guideline: Canadian Paediatric Society (CPS) — bronchiolitis, fever, toxicology, safeguarding and paediatric acute-care guidance.
guidelines.global_standard: Strict monitoring of bronchiolitis with continuous pulse oximetry, avoiding routine bronchodilators.
guidelines.african_reality: Severe shortage of pulse oximeter probes in busy district pediatric wards, forcing clinicians to rely on clinical respiratory work indices.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Relying on accessory muscle use, subcostal recessions, and simple hydration monitoring to guide bronchiolitis disposition.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Without continuous pulse oximetry, we rely on clinical work-of-breathing indices and accessory muscle recessions to safely manage bronchiolitis.
guidelines.bibliography: FINAL DRAFT Paediatric Clinical Protocol - Western Cape Government. Paediatric Meningitis Protocol. 2017.

guidelines.guideline: WHO Emergency Triage, Assessment and Treatment and Basic Emergency Care — especially relevant in resource-constrained settings.
guidelines.global_standard: Identifies severe acute malnutrition (SAM) with dehydration, but historically recommends strictly avoiding IV fluids unless advanced shock is present.
guidelines.african_reality: Fears of sudden congestive cardiac failure with IV fluids. However, ReSoMal is frequently out of stock, making purely oral rehydration impossible [226].
guidelines.local_adaptation: Adapting findings from the GASTROSAM trial: Cautious IV rehydration (100 mL/kg Ringer's Lactate over 3-8 hours) is safe and reduces pediatric mortality.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: While standard WHO guidelines warn against IV fluids in SAM, the GASTROSAM trial proved that cautious IV rehydration (100 mL/kg Ringer's Lactate) is safe and improves survival.
guidelines.bibliography: Gastroenteritis Rehydration Of children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (GASTROSAM). Wellcome Open Res. 2021;6:160.

guidelines.guideline: AHA/ERC paediatric life-support guidelines — paediatric cardiac arrest, shock, respiratory failure and neonatal resuscitation.
guidelines.global_standard: Mandates immediate advanced airway support, real-time feedback devices, and early use of central intraosseous access.
guidelines.african_reality: Intraosseous needles and specialized pediatric airway equipment are frequently unavailable in rural clinics.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Prioritization of high-quality bag-valve-mask (BVM) ventilation, basic airway maneuvers, and prompt peripheral venous access.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Our pediatric life support focuses on basic high-quality BVM ventilation and rapid peripheral access, as advanced airway equipment is often out of stock.
guidelines.bibliography: FINAL DRAFT Paediatric Clinical Protocol - Western Cape Government. Paediatric Meningitis Protocol. 2017.

guidelines.guideline: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Green-top Guidelines — ectopic pregnancy, postpartum haemorrhage, thromboembolism and other obstetric emergencies.
guidelines.global_standard: Routine low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) thromboprophylaxis for all post-delivery patients with high-risk markers.
guidelines.african_reality: Inconsistent enoxaparin supplies in district obstetric units, making universal prophylaxis difficult.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Prioritizing chemical thromboprophylaxis for the highest-risk postnatal patients, utilizing weight-standardized enoxaparin dosing.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Due to enoxaparin resource limits, we prioritize chemical prophylaxis strictly for our highest-risk postnatal cohorts using weight-standardized dosing.
guidelines.bibliography: Standard Treatment Guidelines and Essential Medicines List for South Africa: hospital level, adults, 2024 edition. National Department of Health; 2024.

guidelines.guideline: WHO maternal and perinatal guidance — postpartum haemorrhage, hypertensive disorders, sepsis and emergency maternal care.
guidelines.global_standard: Immediate administration of Carbetocin or Oxytocin infusions with active management of the third stage of labor.
guidelines.african_reality: Oxytocin requires continuous cold chain storage, which is frequently compromised during transport or electrical outages in rural clinics.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Empiric use of oral Misoprostol (600 mcg) or heat-stable Ergometrine formulations where cold chains are unstable.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: When electrical grids compromise oxytocin cold chains, we utilize oral misoprostol or alternative heat-stable formulations for postpartum hemorrhage control.
guidelines.bibliography: Fluids, drugs and transfusion - The Global Library of Women's Medicine. Pregnancy Hypertension. 2015.

guidelines.guideline: International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) — postpartum haemorrhage and other international obstetric consensus recommendations.
guidelines.global_standard: Immediate balloon tamponade or surgical devascularization for severe, refractory postpartum hemorrhage (PPH).
guidelines.african_reality: Uterine balloon tamponade kits are frequently unavailable, and access to emergency obstetric surgery is delayed.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Improvising uterine balloon tamponade using a sterile condom tied to a Foley catheter, filled with 300-500 mL of warm sterile saline.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: To control refractory PPH when commercial kits are unavailable, we utilize an improvised condom-catheter balloon tamponade as a life-saving bridge.
guidelines.bibliography: Fluids, drugs and transfusion - The Global Library of Women's Medicine. Pregnancy Hypertension. 2015.

guidelines.guideline: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) — pregnancy emergencies, hypertension, haemorrhage and early pregnancy complications.
guidelines.global_standard: Recommends intensive intravenous labetalol or hydralazine infusions for severe gestational hypertension.
guidelines.african_reality: Continuous IV infusion pumps are unavailable in secondary EDs, and intravenous access is often difficult.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Adopting the South African ESMOE protocol: Rapid-acting oral Nifedipine (10 mg oral tablet, swallowed whole without biting), and strictly restricting fluids to 80 mL/hour to prevent pulmonary edema [159].
guidelines.rounding_pitch: To manage severe pre-eclampsia and prevent maternal stroke, we administer oral nifedipine and restrict total fluids strictly to 80 mL/hour to avoid pulmonary edema.
guidelines.bibliography: Eclampsia Dr Mandondo. Essential Steps in Managing Obstetric Emergencies (ESMOE) Protocol. Knowledge Hub. 2024.

guidelines.guideline: American Academy of Clinical Toxicology (AACT) — toxicological position statements and decontamination guidance.
guidelines.global_standard: Universal administration of activated charcoal (1 g/kg) within 1 hour of any potentially toxic ingestion.
guidelines.african_reality: In South African primary care, oral N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is used for paracetamol poisonings when referrals are delayed [3]. Activated charcoal binds oral NAC, negating its therapeutic effect [4].
guidelines.local_adaptation: Strictly avoiding activated charcoal if oral NAC is to be administered [4]. The oral NAC regimen is 140 mg/kg loading, followed by 17 doses of 70 mg/kg 4-hourly.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Activated charcoal must be strictly avoided if we are administering oral NAC, as it binds the antidote and negates its life-saving systemic absorption.
guidelines.supporting_evidence: South African National Primary Healthcare EML.
guidelines.bibliography: South African Primary Healthcare Level Essential Medicines List. Chapter 21: Emergencies and Injuries. National Department of Health. 2020.

guidelines.guideline: European Association of Poisons Centres and Clinical Toxicologists (EAPCCT) — joint international toxicology position papers, including activated charcoal and gastrointestinal decontamination.
guidelines.global_standard: Mandates emergency gastric lavage only for life-threatening ingestions presenting within 1 hour.
guidelines.african_reality: In rural settings, gastric lavage is frequently performed late by untrained personnel using inadequate airway protection, risking fatal aspiration.
guidelines.local_adaptation: Strictly avoiding emergency gastric lavage in patients with depressed consciousness or unprotected airways, prioritizing supportive care.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: We strictly prohibit gastric lavage in patients with depressed mental status to prevent fatal aspiration pneumonia, focusing instead on supportive airway care.
guidelines.bibliography: South African Primary Healthcare Level Essential Medicines List. Chapter 21: Emergencies and Injuries. National Department of Health. 2020.

guidelines.guideline: American College of Medical Toxicology (ACMT) — antidotes, envenomation, opioid toxicity, extracorporeal treatment and toxicological practice statements.
guidelines.global_standard: Recommends routine use of pralidoxime or obidoxime (oximes) as essential reactivators in severe organophosphate poisoning.
guidelines.african_reality: Oximes are virtually out of stock or unavailable in almost all South African public hospitals [55].
guidelines.local_adaptation: Focusing entirely on aggressive atropine titration (doubling the dose every 5 minutes) to resolve the cholinergic 'Killer B's' and avoiding apnea-suppressing opioids.
guidelines.rounding_pitch: Because oximes are unavailable, we manage organophosphate poisoning with aggressive atropine titration to clear bronchial secretions, strictly avoiding succinylcholine.
guidelines.bibliography: Approach to Organophosphate Poisoning. National Department of Health. Knowledge Hub. 2024.

landmark_trials.name: FEAST Trial (2011)
landmark_trials.citation: Maitland K, Kiguli S, Opoka RO, et al. Mortality after fluid bolus in African children with severe infection. N Engl J Med. 2011;364(26):2483-2495.
landmark_trials.core_finding: Proved that rapid fluid boluses (20-40 mL/kg) significantly increase 48-hour mortality by 45% in sub-Saharan African children with severe infection and impaired perfusion, compared to conservative maintenance fluids without a bolus.
landmark_trials.rounding_pitch: When the consultant asks about resuscitation in febrile children, cite the FEAST trial. Note that rapid fluid boluses increased relative mortality by 45% because in the absence of mechanical ventilation, aggressive volume expansion overrides the cardiac reserve of a reductively adapted, hyperdynamic heart.

landmark_trials.name: AMBITION-cm Trial (2022)
landmark_trials.citation: Jarvis JN, Lawrence DS, Meya DB, et al. Single-dose liposomal amphotericin B treatment for cryptococcal meningitis. N Engl J Med. 2022;386(12):1109–1120.
landmark_trials.core_finding: Demonstrated that a single high-dose of liposomal amphotericin B (10 mg/kg) on Day 1, combined with 14 days of oral flucytosine and fluconazole, is non-inferior to the older 7-day deoxycholate regimens, while significantly reducing drug-induced anemia, nephrotoxicity, and clinical monitoring costs.
landmark_trials.rounding_pitch: On rounds, cite the AMBITION-cm trial to justify our first-line cryptococcal meningitis induction. A single high-dose of liposomal amphotericin B (10 mg/kg) on Day 1 is safer, cheaper, and non-inferior to deoxycholate regimens, making it our gold standard.

landmark_trials.name: GASTROSAM Trial (2021)
landmark_trials.citation: Maitland K, Gastroenteritis Rehydration Of children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (GASTROSAM): A Phase II Randomised Controlled trial. Wellcome Open Res. 2021;6:160.
landmark_trials.core_finding: Challenged the traditional conservative WHO guidelines that prohibit intravenous fluid rehydration in severely acutely malnourished (SAM) children. Showed that cautious intravenous rehydration (100 mL/kg of standard isotonic Ringer's Lactate over 3 to 8 hours depending on dehydration severity) is safe and significantly improves survival.
landmark_trials.rounding_pitch: When asked about managing dehydrated children with severe acute malnutrition, cite the GASTROSAM trial. It proved that cautious intravenous rehydration (100 mL/kg Ringer's Lactate) is clinically safe, does not trigger heart failure, and improves survival over standard oral ReSoMal.

landmark_trials.name: Magpie Trial (2002)
landmark_trials.citation: The Magpie Trial Collaboration Group. Do women with pre-eclampsia, and their babies, benefit from magnesium sulphate? Lancet. 2002;359(9321):1877–1888.
landmark_trials.core_finding: Established that magnesium sulphate (MgSO4) reduces the relative risk of eclampsia by 58% in women with severe pre-eclampsia, and lowers the risk of maternal death, without causing significant maternal or neonatal adverse effects.
landmark_trials.rounding_pitch: To justify our aggressive seizure prophylaxis in pre-eclampsia, cite the Magpie trial. It proved that magnesium sulphate cuts the risk of eclampsia by 58%, making it our primary first-line intervention in the obstetric emergency department.

landmark_trials.name: CRASH-2 Trial (2010)
landmark_trials.citation: CRASH-2 collaborators. Effects of tranexamic acid on death, vascular occlusive events, and blood transfusion in trauma patients with significant haemorrhage: a randomised, placebo-controlled trial. Lancet. 2010;376(9734):23-32.
landmark_trials.core_finding: Proved that early administration of Tranexamic Acid (TXA) (1 g loading dose over 10 minutes, followed by 1 g infusion over 8 hours) significantly reduces all-cause mortality in bleeding trauma patients, with the greatest benefit achieved when given within 3 hours of injury.
landmark_trials.rounding_pitch: In major trauma resuscitations, cite the CRASH-2 trial. It established that administering 1 g of TXA within 3 hours of injury significantly reduces bleeding-related mortality, meaning we must prioritize prompt delivery directly in the resuscitation bay.
